A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MKDT research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including the new appendices E–F and the societal-impact paragraph moved from E to G.

before.justification: v1 reports original MKDT pre-training, downstream classification, ablation, and architecture-transfer results in Section 5, together with empirical trajectory analysis in Figure 1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds KRR-ST comparison results and downstream evaluations of DM and MTT adapted to SSL.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the proposed procedure remain unchanged: SSL teacher training, MSE-based student trajectories, high-loss initialization, and trajectory matching that optimizes synthetic images and their learning rate while keeping target representations fixed. Appendix F adapts comparison methods, not MKDT.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and TinyImageNet for pre-training, with the same downstream classification datasets, including Aircraft, CUB2011, Dogs, Flowers, and Cars in Appendix B. The additions evaluate existing coverage without introducing new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 4–7 newly include KRR-ST in comparisons involving 5% distilled sets, ResNet transfer, SimCLR, and larger labeled fractions. Appendix F adds label-free DM comparisons and extends MTT-SSL from Figure 1's trajectory analysis to downstream accuracy comparisons in Tables 11–12. This substantially broadens comparator participation.

E3.justification: Table 8 changes the reported maximum start epoch for 2% CIFAR10 distillation from 2 to 5; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Appendix F also introduces comparison procedures using dataset-wide sampling for DM and SimCLR for MTT's expert trajectories and inner-loop training. Existing evaluation metrics and labeled-data fractions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds downstream checks of whether removing class-based sampling from DM or using SSL trajectories in MTT enables effective distillation, extending the earlier failure analysis. Appendix E provides comparative image examples. The existing initialization, SSL-algorithm, batch-size, and architecture analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing ± accuracy reporting and the five trajectories specified for Figure 1 remain unchanged. New result rows follow the same reporting practice, without new seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All pre-existing accuracy entries in Tables 1–7 and 10 are retained, but KRR-ST results in Tables 4–7 and DM/MTT-SSL results in Tables 11–12 substantially expand the comparative findings. For example, Table 6 now reports Flowers accuracy of 2.35±0.06 for KRR-ST with CIFAR10 pre-training and 1% labels, exceeding the retained MKDT entry of 1.88±0.22.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Theorem 4.1, Proposition D.1, and their proofs in appendices C–D retain the same assumptions, equations, and reasoning. Changes to citations and wording about the simplified theoretical setting do not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that MKDT enables effective SSL dataset distillation through lower-variance KD trajectories, achieves up to 13% higher accuracy, and transfers across architectures and SSL algorithms. Naming ResNet-18 more explicitly does not materially change the existing contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 qualifies the theoretical support for trajectory variance from 'confirmed theoretically' to 'illustrated theoretically in the simplified setting,' modestly softening the interpretation. The variance mechanism, explanation for larger models' weaker performance, and societal bias limitation otherwise remain unchanged; the societal-impact paragraph is merely relocated.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link in the abstract and explains that KRR-ST's CIFAR10 experiment reuses CIFAR100 hyperparameters and a BarlowTwins ResNet-18 teacher. Appendix F documents the baseline adaptations, and Table 8 revises one hyperparameter. The KRR-ST clarification documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a changed procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Lopes et al. (2017) and Shao et al. (2024), connecting statistical distribution matching to data-free knowledge distillation. The Qiu et al. (2023) reference disappears, and the introduction's SimCLR attribution is corrected to the already-cited Chen et al. (2020). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 switches to author–year citations and an ICLR publication header, makes limited wording corrections, expands implementation explanations, and inserts appendices E–F before the relocated societal-impact section. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds paired MKDT/KRR-ST image grids for three datasets in Figures 2–4, adds Tables 11–12, and expands Tables 4–7 with comparator rows. These substantially extend the visual presentation and redistribute existing tables. Figure 1's plots remain identical despite relocation.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, distilled-image examples, and implementation disclosures modestly strengthen empirical support and transparency while preserving the method and existing results. Integration remains imperfect: Section 5 still says the 5% experiments include only Random and MKDT despite the added KRR-ST rows, and Appendix F describes CIFAR100-only distillation despite also reporting CIFAR10 rows. These inconsistencies limit the gains, but the broader evidence provides a net improvement.
